articleTitle: Radiation Evaluation of a Dual D-Type Flip-Flop with Triple Modular Redundancy
abstract: Single Events Effect (SEE) characterization results for a Dual D-Type Flip-Flop with Triple Modular Redundancy is summarized, showing very robust SEE performance up to LET<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EFF</inf>=75 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg. A comparison is made between a device with TMR (Triple Modular Redundancy) & a device without TMR to showcase the SEE performance differences.

articleTitle: Assessment of Advanced Non-Volatile Fefet Memories Based on Hafnium-Oxide
abstract: The ESA project<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>European Space Agency contract number 4000132931/20/NL/FE “Assessment of Advanced NonVolatile Memories” is about the identification and evaluation of emerging non-volatile memory technology for future missions. A detailed market analysis and literature review have been conducted and Ferroelectric Hafnium-Oxid FET (FeFET) has been selected as very promising technology. Thereof, a prototype memory IC has been designed and manufactured that underwent functional, thermal and radiation testing. In summary, the goals of the de-risk activity have been achieved and the feasibility of utilizing FeFET technology in space environment has been demonstrated. This NVM technology will be well suited for future applications as companion memory to processors or comparable.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effect of 14 MeV Neutrons on Google Coral EdgeAI
abstract: This work studies the influence of 14 MeV neutron radiation on a commercial of-the-shelf tensor processing unit. The device under test was a Google Coral USB accelerator for edge artificial intelligence operations running pre-trained models. Three different neural networks were investigated, two image classification models of different size and complexity and one semantic segmentation model. The errors in both software and hardware resulting from irradiation were assessed across all three models. It has been demonstrated that the cross sections of the soft errors depends on the model, where the larger and more complex models show higher cross sections. Nevertheless, all observed soft errors only led to minor changes in the output and no misclassifications or serious incorrect segmentations were observed. Furthermore, cross sections were calculated for hardware errors. Despite their smaller values than those associated with soft errors, they could result in complete hardware failure. These findings underscore the importance of a detailed comprehension of neutron radiation effects on edge devices to ensure the component's resistance to radiation-induced malfunctions. Subsequent efforts will prioritize a deeper understanding of the failure mechanisms in different models, aiming to enhance the durability and resistance of these devices when operating within challenging radiation environments.

articleTitle: Effects of Proton Energy on Optocoupler Displacement Damage Tests
abstract: This article presents the degradation data collected from five optocouplers during proton displacement damage tests performed at three proton energies within 15-190 MeV. In most cases, the intermediate proton energy is the worst test condition.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects Characterization of COTS Components to be Used as Protection Devices
abstract: This paper reports recent Single-Event Effects test results on a selection of COTS intended to be used as protection device: overcurrent, overvoltage and watchdog devices. This study was motivated by ESA to identify COTS protection devices immune to destructive Single Event Effects that could benefit the European space community. Out of the 12 tested COTS references, only 4 were not sensitive to SEL or other destructive SEE.

articleTitle: Guide to the 2022 RADECS Radiation Effects Data Session
abstract: The 2022 RADECS Data Workshop Session has been reviewed and a table prepared to facilitate the search for radiation response data by part number, type, or effect.

articleTitle: Proton Radiation Test of Gamma-Ray Transients Monitor (GTM) on Board Formosat-8B
abstract: The Gamma-ray Transients Monitor (GTM) is a secondary payload on board Formosat-8B (FS-8B), a Taiwanese remote-sensing satellite, to monitor Gamma Ray Bursts (GRBs) and other bright gamma-ray transients in the energy range from 50 keV to 2 MeV. The readout module of GTM was built with all commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components to meet very restricted power and size requirements, including frontend analog devices, switching and linear regulators, interface devices and field programmable gate array (FPGA). Therefore, a 221 MeV proton radiation test in the Proton and Radiation Therapy Center of Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, Taiwan was conducted to ensure the reliability of GTM readout module operated in the low earth orbit (LEO) environment. The accumulated 221 MeV proton fluence in this test was 1.03×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> proton/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, equivalent to 5.6 krad(Si), with average proton flux 2.50×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> proton/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/sec. There was not any catastrophic event observed in this proton radiation test. Only soft error events were seen with reasonably low cross-sections.

articleTitle: Single Event Upset Characterization of the Polarfire® SoC RISC-V Microprocessor SubSystem Using Proton Irradiation
abstract: The proton induced SEU cross-section of the Polarfire® SoC RISC-V Microprocessor SubSystem is presented. Upset rate in the space radiation environment is estimated.

articleTitle: Data Pattern Dependence of the Total Ionizing Dose Effect in 3D Nand Flash Memories
abstract: The total ionizing dose effect (TID) is one of radiation effects that must semiconductor chips for outer space use. We have evaluated the TID characteristics for each data pattern in triple level cell (TLC) floating-gate and charge-trap NAND flash memories. Gamma-ray irradiation measurements showed that the TID characteristics of the charge-trap type depend more on the data pattern than those of the floating-gate type. The chargetrap type has high TID tolerance for data patterns with small cell threshold voltages shifts, but the tolerance significantly decreases as the threshold voltage increases.

articleTitle: Built-In Self-Test Measurement of Single Event Transients in the Skywater S90ln 90 Nm Process
abstract: Heavy-ion-induced single-event transients (SET) in combinational logic gates fabricated in the SkyWater S90LN 90 nm bulk CMOS process are measured experimentally using programmable built-in self-test (BIST) circuits. Four BIST circuits, differing only in the type of combinational logic gates, were simultaneously irradiated at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory 88” Cyclotron facility using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16 \text{MeV} / \text{amu}$</tex> ion cocktail and a range of linear energy transfer (LET) values. The median SET pulse widths for minimally-sized inverters and those up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 x$</tex> the minimum drive strength range between 70 and 630 ps, whereas the minimally-sized two-input NAND gates showed median pulse widths between 210 ps and 960 ps for LET values up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$67 \text{MeV}-\text{cm}^{2} / \text{mg}$</tex>. For LET values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30 \text{MeV}-\text{cm}^{2} / \text{mg}$</tex> or less, nearly all SET pulse widths are contained to within 1 ns, with the maximum SET pulse width being 1.96 ns for the two-input NAND gates measured at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$67 \text{MeV}-\text{cm}^{2} / \text{mg}$</tex>. Further, cross-sections tend to be inversely proportional to drive strength, as expected.

articleTitle: Nor-Flash Memories Under Protons and Neutrons
abstract: Commercial NOR-Flash memories were written with several patterns at different bias voltages and irradiated with protons and neutrons in order to know the effect of the bias voltage on the single event cross sections. No conclusive related results were found, but weird single event functional interrupts were observed.

articleTitle: Dose Rate Effects on Dynamic Operation of an 8-Bit Microcontroller
abstract: This work presents dose rate testing of an 8-bit microcontroller which executes code during radiation pulses. Multiple different failure modes are observed, which depend on the dose rate and integrated dose received by the device.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose Response of Cots Operational Amplifiers
abstract: Total Ionizing Dose response of four different COTS operational amplifiers were evaluated using low dose rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ }^{60}$</tex> Co irradiation. Results shown they were all tolerant to 30 krad.

articleTitle: SAMD21RT 32-Bits ARM Cortex-M0+ Microcontroller Single Event Effects & TID Evaluation
abstract: This paper reports the results of Single Event Effects (SEE) and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) test campaigns conducted by Microchip on the ARM® Cortex® M0+ SAMD21RT Microcontroller

articleTitle: Up-Screening of NVE IL611 Digital Isolator
abstract: The Compliant Assistance and Exploration SpAce Robot (CAESAR) is the space qualified equivalent to the current service robot systems for manufacturing and human-robot cooperation. It was developed by the Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and is designed for a variety of on-orbit services e.g. assembly, maintenance, repair, and debris removal in LEO/GEO. It is used within the European Robotic Orbital Support Services In Orbit Demonstrator (EROSS IOD) mission. Crucial for the operation of the robotic arm is the central power unit which have to fulfill multiple requirements of the robotic arm and of the spacecraft on the other hand. Since the design of the Base Power and Isolation Unti (BPIU) is such, that the primary power domain of the Spacecraft is galvanically isolated from the secondary power domain, digital signals e.g. for retrieving housekeeping information have to be routed through this isolation barrier which requires digital isolators. These parts are able to withstand a voltage difference between both power domains and transmit a digital signal from one domain to the other. Within the current BPIU design, the tested digital isolator IL611 from NVE shall be used for this task. Therefore, the part was screened for Total Ionizing Dose (TID) initially. Afterwards a Proton Test and a Heavy Ion Test were conducted. This paper highlights the most important results of the conducted tests.

articleTitle: See Test Results of Critical Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (Cots) Electronic Components for a Low Earth Orbit Radiation Monitor
abstract: COTS electronic components intended for being used in the Home-Grown Radiation Monitor were tested under 15 MeV and 30 MeV proton irradiation at METU-DBL and with 60 MeV protons at UCLouvain CRC. The resulting single event effects (SEE) on the components and their analyses are presented

articleTitle: Low-Energy Proton Displacement Damage on Optocouplers at CNA
abstract: This research explores the impact of low-energy proton displacement damage on five optocouplers used in space applications, employing the cyclotron accelerator at the Centro Nacional de Aceleradores for the first time within this group.

articleTitle: Tid and See Response of the Dc2386a-B Wireless Power Transfer Module.
abstract: Performance degradation of the DC2386A-B Wireless Power Transfer Module was studied using low dose rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{60} \text{Co}$</tex> irradiation. SEE response was evaluated using a 105 MeV proton beam. Results revealed the Module is TID and SEE, tolerant.

articleTitle: Compendium of Total Ionizing Dose Tests of Commercial-Off-The-Shelf Components (Part 2)
abstract: This paper addresses the radiation characterization and functional verification of COTS components for space applications

articleTitle: Compendium of TID and SEE Data on Discrete Flip-Flop and Logic Gate Devices
abstract: This paper presents a compendium of Total Ionizing Dose (TID) and Single Event Effects (SEE) test data gathered on several references of logic components: D-type flip-flops (DFFs), configurable logic gates (CLGs) and NAND gates.

articleTitle: Proton See Characterization of Nexus CertusPro-NX FPGA Implementing GRLIB LEON3FT-based System-on-Chip
abstract: This work presents the proton SEE characterization of the Lattice 28nm FDSOI Nexus CertusPro-NX FPGA implementing a Frontgrade Gaisler GRLIB LEON3FT-based system-on-chip. The effectiveness of the device's built-in scrubber and processor's fault tolerance features in coping with soft errors on both the configuration and user memories, respectively, have been demonstrated.

articleTitle: TID Characterization for a Ka-Band Capable, Low Power, 10 Bits ADC
abstract: EV10AS940 is a 10-bit single channel Analog-toDigital Converter (ADC) capable of Ka-band operation, enabling a sampling rate up to 12.8GSps, with power consumption no more than 2.5W. The EV10AS940 is packaged with an organic substrate to allow high speed and high bandwidth operations. This paper presents the results of TID tests carried out in 2023 to validate its adaptation to a harsh space environment. The measurements were carried out at TRAD (Labège, France) using the GAMRAY irradiation facility. The parts have received a total dose of 100krad at a dose rate of 325 rad/h. After irradiation, the annealing procedure was followed. Throughout the test, the main parameters of the device were measured with a test bench. The measurements involved monitoring power consumption as well as ENOB, SNR, THD and SFDR parameters for different input powers. The results show that the device behaved perfectly throughout the test, with no significant variations. This campaign proves the chip is perfectly suited for the long duration space applications.

Author Keywords: High-Speed Analog to Digital Broadband Data Converter

articleTitle: Single Event Effects on a Highly Integrated and RF Agile Wideband Transceiver Device
abstract: This paper presents the single event effects (SEE) test results of the latest highly integrated and radio frequency (RF) agile wideband transceiver, namely the Analog Devices ADRV9009. The test was performed under heavy-ion irradiation. The ADRV9009 is a very complex device which combines digital, analog and RF circuits. The test results revealed that multiple kinds of SEE occur on all circuit levels. Destructive events, driven by single event latchups were observed at Krypton and Xenon with an LET of 40.9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MeV} \cdot \text{cm}^{2} / \text{mg}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$69.3 \text{MeV} \cdot \text{cm}^{2} / \text{mg}$</tex> respectively. Soft errors like single event upsets in the configuration memory, the integrated ARM processor and signal disruption and connection losses in the RF domain were observed down to a LET of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.17 \text{MeV} \cdot \text{cm}^{2} / \text{mg}$</tex>.

articleTitle: TID and SEE Results of Various COTS Parts and the Lessons Learned From the ESA-CORHA Project
abstract: We present investigations on total ionizing dose (TID) and Single Event Effects (SEE) radiation testing of various commercial devices (microcontroller, ADC, operational amplifier, multiplexer) as part of the ESA CORHA study. Furthermore, we compile the lessons learned of COTS testing gathered within the CORHA study that is performed on a comprehensive COTs sample set in TID and SEE radiation environments.

articleTitle: Effects of Proton and Gamma Radiation on DDR4 SDRAM in Elevated Temperature
abstract: This paper shows that various types of soft errors such as SBU, SEFI and SEL occurs in DDR4 SDRAMs using cutting edge technology node due to proton radiation in hot temperature. The failure rate by error types were compared between manufacturers. Some of SBU did not recover even after radiation was stopped. It was confirmed that the refresh characteristics of most DRAM cells were deteriorated due to radiation.

articleTitle: Radiation Characterization of the Cots Myriad X Edge Vision Processing Unit and Use Cases in Space Applications
abstract: This work presents the radiation characterization of the COTS Myriad X Vision Processing Unit, from Intel Movidius, for proton- and heavy ion-induced Single Event Effects and Total Ionizing Dose. The component has already flown on different missions, and it continues to be considered in future ones. The results obtained show that the radiation performance of the device is aligned with the performance of other components manufactured in the 16nm FinFET technology. Potential use cases of Myriad X in space computing platforms are also discussed.

articleTitle: Compendium of Total Ionizing Dose Tests of Commercial-off-the-Shelf Components (Part 1)
abstract: This paper addresses the radiation characterization and functional verification of COTS components for space applications

articleTitle: Single Event Effects (SEE), Laser, and Total Dose (TID) Testing for AFP1422 Flexible PWM Controller
abstract: This paper covers the Heavy Ion Single Event Effects (SEE), Laser, and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) testing completed on the AFP1422 Radiation Hardened PWM Controller. SEE testing included Single Event Transient (SET) testing up to an effective LET of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4 0. 4 ~ M e V * c m 2 / m g. }$</tex> Laser testing was initially completed via topside exposure and later completed through the backside of the device using a beam with energy up to 1.5 nJ. TID testing was completed with bias conditions up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300 \text{krad}(\text{Si})$</tex>.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose Characterization of Advanced Latch-Up Current Limiter ASIC
abstract: This paper presents the results of the Total Ionizing Dose characterization of the Analog Current Control Loop implemented within the SKY-IC-RHLCL-A1 Latch-Up current limiter application-specific integrated circuit. Given the criticality of Single Event Latch-ups in satellite platforms, the use of safeguard circuits such as latching current limiters is essential. This work focuses on performance and resilience of the Analog Current Control Loop, which is responsible for the measurements of protected load current and current limitation in case of a Single Event Latch-up. The characterization results provide valuable insights into the behavior and reliability of the Latch-up current limiter under the irradiation exposure. Five out of six biased current limiters were able to function up to 40 krad(Si) of Total Ionizing Dose, whereas one experienced failure at 22 krad(Si) due to startup circuit failure. Beyond 40 krad(Si), the devices began to fail gradually, but regained functionality after the annealing process.

articleTitle: SEL and SEU In-Flight Data from Memories on-board PROBA-II Spacecraft
abstract: This paper presents an update of the SEE in-flight data of memories on board Proba-II spacecraft. Proba-II spacecraft has been flying on a LEO orbit since November 2009. Observed in-flight error rates are compared with predictions based on ground test data.

articleTitle: TID Radiation Characterization of a Commercial High-Speed Delay Line
abstract: The Kepler concept proposed by the German Aerospace Center (DLR) intends to drastically improve the performance and robustness of the European Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Galileo. To do so, Kepler relies on ultra-precise optical time transfer and ranging between the satellites of the GNSS constellation. Accuracy down to picosecond-level in time transfer can be reached by employing broadband delay lines in the satellites' electronics. Delay lines are integrated circuits capable of applying a precise and controllable time delay to signals. This class of components is currently not available in space-grade and it is therefore necessary to characterize the behavior of such devices in a radiation environment before considering their usage in orbit. The purpose of this work is to investigate the effects of total ionizing dose (TID) on a commercial high-speed delay line. Co-60 is used as gamma ray source. Total doses of 15 krad in low dose rate and of 300 krad in high dose rate are reached.

articleTitle: Radiation Evaluation of the Texas Instruments TPS7H3014-SP Radiation Hardened Four-Channel Power-supply Sequencer
abstract: Single events effect (SEE) characterization and total ionizing dose (TID) results for the TPS7H3014-SP 14-V integrated four-channel sequencer are summarized, showing very powerful SEE performance up to LET<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EFF</inf>=75 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg and excellent TID behavior.

articleTitle: Impact of Technology Node on Soft Error Sensitivity of Flip-Flops and Srams in St Bcd Technology
abstract: In this work, we explore and compare ST BCD technology platform robustness against soft errors induced by alpha particles, neutrons and heavy-ions on both Flip-Flops and SRAMs ranging from the available 110 nm node up to the most advanced and under development 40 nm node.

articleTitle: Optocouplers Behavior Analysis on Neutron Displacement Damage
abstract: In this work, the degradation on a series of selected optocouplers is evaluated under neutron displacement damage (DD) testing. New experimental data have been statistically analyzed using the PRECEDER methodology.

articleTitle: Quad Core Processor Level-2 Cache Verification Using a Californium-252 Source
abstract: During the design phase of a fault-tolerant LEON4 quad-core processor ASIC for space applications, a Californium <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$252\left({}^{252} \text{Cf}\right)$</tex> source was used to inject errors on the memory cells of a test vehicle to verify the error correction scheme embedded in the Level-1 (L1) and Level-2 (L2) cache of the processors. An issue, that could have caused a significant detrimental effect on the radiation performance of the processor, was identified, and delimited to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{L 2}$</tex> cache. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{252} \mathbf{C f}$</tex> source allowed the authors to do a quick validation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L 2$</tex> cache, to test a software workaround and kick-off a new revision of the chip. Breaking tradition, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{252}$</tex> Cf source was used as an alpha emitter instead of a heavy ion emitter. This work aims at showing that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{252} \text{Cf}$</tex> sources, long disused for SEE testing, may still be useful for the injection of SEUs in the memory cells of submicron ICs. Error maps generated with alpha particles are also compared against proton and heavy ion's induced error maps.

articleTitle: Upgrading Optocoupler Experimental Data on DD Neutron Radiation Testing
abstract: We present a compendium of data obtained from the neutron Displacement Damage (DD) test campaigns on 27 different optocouplers. These experimental data will be used to analyse the degradation of the most sensitive parameters.

articleTitle: Radiation Induced Single Events and Cumulated Dose Effects on CMOS and InGaAs Image Sensors
abstract: This article presents irradiation tests performed by CNES on several SONY, AMS-OSRAM, TELEDYNE-E2V and PYXALIS commercial CMOS image sensors, as well as SONY InGaAs image sensors.

articleTitle: Simulation and Radiation Measurements from Three Stratospheric Balloon Flights
abstract: Atmospheric showers, produced by radiation from space that hit the higher layers of the atmosphere, propagate through it and produce effects on both electronic systems and living beings. They have been analyzed in depth at aeronautical heights, for their impacts on airplanes, passengers and crews, but now they are becoming more important at stratospheric altitudes, where new scientific and communications missions operate. This abstract summarizes the measurements taken by three radiation monitors flying through the Stratosphere on board three scientific balloons. We also developed a series of simulations with FLUKA to better understand the interaction of the radiation with the monitor and to determine the impact of the monitor shielding on the detection capabilities. Further work will be needed to discriminate types of particles and energy levels, and to study in detail such measurements. But we can show now the fluxes of ionizing particles measured by our monitors while flying over Sweden, Canada and Spain from the ground to altitudes of about 35 km. Thanks to the simulations performed it is possible to know the minimum necessary energy for the incoming particle to go through the external thermal insulation box of the monitor and reach its electronic to be measured.

articleTitle: Heavy-Ion Radiation Test on LTC1668 DAC
abstract: We measured the heavy ion-induced single-event effect (SEE) susceptibility of the LTC1668 DAC from Linear Technology, to be used in the LiteBIRD JAXA space mission. LiteBIRD will be operated from the Lagrangian L2 in the early 30s, to map the microwave sky with three telescopes equipped with ~ 4800 Transition Edge Sensors (TES) distributed onto three focal planes. The DAC we investigate here is a key item of the detector readout chain since it generates the MHz bias signal that is required by the TES Frequency-Division Multiplexing scheme. This 16 -bit/50 Msps DAC has been identified as a critical element by its output spectral purity and low-power consumption (180 mW), which allow us to fulfil LiteBIRD's power budget constraints. Since this device doesn't exist in a space-qualified version, we have carried out a first characterization campaign at the heavy-ion facility Tandem-ALPI at INFN Legnaro National Laboratory (Italy) for a total irradiation time of ~ 51 hours, to investigate its susceptibility to SEE. We have exposed the device to a beam of different ions with LET values ranging from 12 to 90 MeV cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. The device is moderately sensitive to SEE, with a threshold LET of 10.3 ± 1.3 MeV cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> for SEU, 7.6 ± 2.0 MeV cm mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> for SEL, and 9.2 ± 1.95 MeV cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> for SET. This first campaign suggests that the use of DAC LTC1668 from space can be seriously considered.

articleTitle: Welcome to the Record of the 2024 Data Workshop Session of the 2024 Conference on Radiation Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The Data Workshop (DW) is an important event allowing researchers to present high quality data about radiation effects on electronics, and to make them available to the community via a dedicated publication. Most of the workshop deals with actual experimental radiation data collected on commercial or radiation hardened parts. Nevertheless, papers presenting facilities used for radiation effects testing as well as simulation data with the purpose of simulating radiation effects and environments are also welcome. The DW is held as a dedicated poster session as part of the yearly Conference on Radiation Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS) Technical Program. The DW poster presenters are also invited to write a paper covering their work. The papers are written in the IEEE Transactions format and until this year they were included in the RADECS Proceedings.
